extracted.intended_audience: Researchers preparing letters of inquiry and full proposals for the William T. Grant Foundation Research Grants on Reducing Inequality (applicants to this foundation program)
extracted.subtask_short: writing letters of inquiry for research grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and review criteria for preparing letters of inquiry (5-page mini-proposals) and, if invited, full proposals for the Foundation's Research Grants on Reducing Inequality program. Covers eligibility, required application elements, formatting, review criteria, and desirable project features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify a specific inequality in youth outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must identify a specific inequality in youth outcomes (academic, social, behavioral, or economic) for young people ages 5–25 in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that outcomes are unequal in a brief discussion of existing literature; highlight the main explanations for the unequal outcomes that are relevant for your study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make a convincing case for the dimension(s) of inequality addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a convincing case for the dimension(s) of inequality the study will address, especially along race, ethnicity, economic standing, sexual or gender minority status, language minority status, or immigrant origin status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be very specific in naming the groups on which the study will focus (avoid vague terms such as 'at-risk youth' or 'vulnerable youth'); offer a well-developed conceptualization of inequality rather than treating dimensions as mere variables; research focusing on other dimensions must be in intersection with one of the listed dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articulate how findings will build/test/increase understanding of a program/policy/practice (theory of change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate how findings from the research will help build, test, or increase understanding of a program, policy, or practice to reduce the identified inequality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw on extant theoretical and empirical literature to provide a rationale for why the specific programs, policies, or practices under study will equalize outcomes or improve outcomes for a particular group; specify your theory of change and identify how the study will investigate this rationale empirically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Information (required fields and brief description limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of inquiry must include project title, start and end dates, total requested amount (including combined direct and indirect costs), and a brief description (1,500 characters maximum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect costs may not exceed 15 percent of total direct costs. For the brief description: start with the major research questions or aims; briefly summarize the project's rationale and background; describe the research methods, data analysis plan, and intervention (if applicable); use language appropriate for an educated lay audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum Vitae / Biographical Sketch / Resume requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a one-page curriculum vitae, biographical sketch, or resume for each Principal Investigator and Co-Principal Investigator (one page maximum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include education and training, peer-reviewed publications, and grants. Do not submit full curricula vitae or resumes. No specific formatting required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative format and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Project narrative is limited to five pages for letters of inquiry and must follow formatting: 12-point Times New Roman font, single-spaced text with a line space between paragraphs, numbered pages, and 1-inch margins on all sides. Reference list, if included, is not counted toward the five-page maximum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the major research questions or aims; provide a strong rationale including a brief literature review, theories that provide the organizing frame, and description of relevance for policy or practice; include specific hypotheses and/or research questions; describe methods and data collection plan (sample/case definition and selection procedures, research design, key constructs, data sources, procedures, and intervention if applicable); summarize the data analysis plan (identify key measures); for quantitative causal analyses provide convincing evidence of adequate power (especially for subgroups); for qualitative data describe coding processes and the plan for establishing coding reliability; for measure development discuss validity and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officers' research grants LOI additional submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of inquiry for Officers' research grants must include a budget and a budget justification form (templates provided in the online application) and the applicant organization's IRS tax-exempt status determination letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect costs for Officers' research grants may not exceed 15 percent of total direct costs. These materials are not required for major research grants letters of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are made only to tax-exempt organizations; the Foundation does not make grants to individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation encourages proposals from organizations under-represented among grantee institutions (HBCUs, Hispanic-serving Institutions, Tribal Colleges and Universities, Alaska Native-Serving Institutions, Native Hawaiian-Serving Institutions, AANHPI-serving institutions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Principal Investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: The applying organization determines who may act as Principal Investigator or Co-Principal Investigator; investigators should have the experience and skills to carry out the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation strives to support a diverse group of researchers by race, ethnicity, gender, and seniority and encourages projects led by Black or African American, Indigenous, Latinx, and/or Asian or Pacific Islander American researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Eligible Studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Only studies that (1) align with the program's stated research interests and (2) relate to the outcomes of young people ages 5–25 in the United States are eligible for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation does not support non-research activities such as program implementation, operational costs, fundraising, endowments, general operating budgets, or scholarships. Letters of inquiry for ineligible projects are screened out without further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use accessible language and avoid disciplinary jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of inquiry should avoid disciplinary jargon and use language appropriate for an educated lay audience because internal reviewers may lack deep knowledge of applicants' specific areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some letters of inquiry will also be reviewed by a panel of youth reviewers in addition to staff, reinforcing the need for clarity and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion: Fit with Research Interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate whether the proposed study aligns with the program's research interests: building, testing, or increasing understanding of programs, policies, or practices to reduce inequality in youth outcomes and focusing on specified dimensions of inequality (or in intersection with them).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies that primarily document causes and consequences of inequality are not a fit. The letter must make clear how findings will inform policies, practices, or programs implementable through organizations, institutions, and/or systems. Inequality may be reduced via approaches that disproportionately help disadvantaged students or via universal approaches applied strategically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion: Conceptualization and Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of inquiry must reflect mastery of relevant theory and empirical findings and state the theoretical and empirical contributions the study will make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how findings will be relevant to policy or practice; show how the project complements and advances existing theory and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion: Methods — rigor and alignment with goals
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed study must employ rigorous quantitative, qualitative, or mixed methods commensurate with its goals, and the study's design, methods, and analysis plan must align with the research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions should make clear how empirical work will test, refine, or elaborate specific theoretical notions. Quantitative proposals should emphasize hypotheses and testing; qualitative proposals should elaborate how research illuminates processes underlying programs, policies, or practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion: Methods — case selection, sampling, and measurement appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for case selection, sampling, and measurement must clearly state why they are well-suited to address the research questions or hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samples must be appropriate in size and composition; qualitative case selection (critical, comparative, etc.) must be appropriate to answer proposed questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion: Methods — analysis plan, strengths/limits, and mixed methods integration
rubrics_metrics.description: The quantitative and/or qualitative analysis plan must show awareness of the strengths and limits of the analytic techniques and how they will be applied; mixed-methods plans must clearly and compellingly integrate methods and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where relevant, discuss potential generalizability of findings and demonstrate consideration of gender, ethnic, and cultural appropriateness of concepts, methods, and measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion: Statistical power for quantitative analyses and subgroup detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative proposals must demonstrate that the study will have adequate statistical power to detect effects, particularly for any subgroups of interest (e.g., differences between different racial and ethnic groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide convincing evidence of adequate power in the letter of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion: Feasibility (methods, timeline, staffing, resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed methods, time frame, staffing plan, and other resources must be realistic and feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assure that data will be successfully collected; describe the team's prior experience collecting such data; identify strategies for maximizing response rates and access to data sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criterion: Team capacity, roles, and track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior training and publications should demonstrate the research team has a track record of conducting strong research and communicating it successfully; the team must be well-positioned to address the study's tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about the value of each member's contributions at different project stages. The Foundation strongly discourages teams comprising many senior investigators with very limited time and effort or cursory multi-disciplinary nods; clearly justify unique value of each team member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valued project features (preferred attributes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects that harness mixed methods and interdisciplinary work, involve practitioners or policymakers meaningfully, combine senior and junior staff for mentoring, are led by underrepresented researchers, generate data useful to others, or demonstrate creativity and potential to advance the field are especially valued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of creativity include introducing new research paradigms or extending methods, measures, and analytic tools to allow for comparison across studies; meaningful practitioner/policymaker involvement should shape questions, interpretation, and communication of implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special interest: Research addressing systemic racism and structural foundations of inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation is particularly interested in research that uproots systemic racism and the structural foundations of inequality, shifting change from individuals to macro-level social institutions and examining how institutions might be altered to dislodge deep roots of inequality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies might examine structural responses, mechanisms of change, shifts in power structures, social movements, reparations, school finance reforms, prosecutorial changes, equitable bank lending policies, or reallocation of municipal resources. Such studies must still focus on youth outcomes ages 5–25 in the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process and full-proposal requirements (if invited)
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful LOIs for major research grants lead to invitations to submit full proposals; the full proposal follows a similar format with a proposal narrative of about 25 pages, a complete budget and budget justification, and full CVs/resumes for key investigators and staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval is not required at submission but is required before issuing grant funds. Full proposals are reviewed by two or more external peer reviewers; applicants may be asked to provide written responses to critiques; final funding decisions involve Senior Program Team review and Board of Trustees approval. Timelines from LOI to funding decision typically range 10–15 months for major grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and submission constraints (page limits, font, margins, references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of inquiry must adhere to explicit formatting and length constraints: five-page project narrative; one-page CVs; 1,500-character brief description; specified font and margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project narrative: 12-point Times New Roman, single-spaced with a blank line between paragraphs, numbered pages, 1-inch margins. Reference list is not counted toward five-page maximum.
